description.value: Prospective fMRI study examining emotional reactivity to sad versus neutral films as a neural predictor of depressive relapse in remitted unipolar depression.

spans.text: Reported here is a prospective functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) analysis method for detecting relapse risk.

description.value: Prospective observational study of remitted unipolar depressed participants and healthy controls with an 18-month follow-up for relapse.

spans.text: Both dorsal and ventral aspects of mPFC reactivity predicted relapse, consistent with suggestions that, in depression, dorsal task-oriented processing becomes linked to ventral self-evaluative processing in the mPFC ( ).

definition.value: In the medial prefrontal region, the most reliable predictor was located on the border of the anterior cingulate and ventral medial prefrontal cortex.

spans.text: In the medial prefrontal region, the most reliable predictor was located on the border of the anterior cingulate and ventral medial prefrontal cortex [ r (14) = .68, p < .005; mPFC; BA 24/32, at peak height: x = 8; y = 38, z = 10], whereas in the visual cortices, the most reliable predictor was located in the left calcarine sulcus, which negatively predicted relapse [ r (14) = –.73, p < .001; BA 37; at peak height: x = –24; y = –64; z = 14].
